newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel to urge full forex liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel to urge full forex liberalisation.

text.p: A key Japanese government panel will urge the Finance Ministry to completely open up foreign exchange transactions when it submits a report on deregulation this week, sources within the ministry said on Tuesday.
Back in June the committee had called for an expansion of the participants allowed to carry out forex businesses and had been discussing the qualifications for the new participants.
"What's different from June is that the new report will say the qualifications for those allowed to conduct forex business should be scrapped altogether," said one MOF source.
The report is scheduled to be released on Thursday.
"We believe the report has taken the deregulatory measures a step or two further from June," added another MOF source.

A subcommittee of the Committee on Foreign Exchange and Other Transactions, an advisory panel to the finance minister, will hold a meeting on Thursday and will agree on the final shape of the report, the sources said.

The committee as a whole will then draft a report detailing the revision of foreign exchange laws, which will then be submitted to the ordinary session of parliament in January, the sources said. The revision will be to implement deregulation measures recommended by the committee.
In addition to a call to open up the forex business to those other than authorised banks, the committee said at the time that the amendments to the law would simplify reporting requirements.
Japanese officials have for a long time limited forex transactions to authorised commercial banks and required them to submit various reports concerning the transactions.
If revised, it will be the first change in Japan's foreign exchange transaction laws in 16 years. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-5473-3710
